title: Summo model manifest
description: One file fully describing one model: where it lives, what it costs, and under what terms.

id.description: Also used as a path segment, hence the restricted character set.

mode.description: live streams with constant cost per chunk; batch is driven by re-decoding a growing window.

langs.description: ISO codes, or ["*"] for language-independent models.

redistributable.description: false means Summo may not host these files; the manifest must point upstream.

rtf.description: Real-time factor keyed by hardware class, e.g. cpu_x86_avx512vnni_8t.

quality.description: Keyed by benchmark, e.g. wer_fleurs_vi. Language-specific keys are preferred when ranking.

name.description: A bare file name; anything path-like is rejected.

platform.description: Restricts a file to one platform, e.g. linux-x64. Omit for portable files.

archive.description: Unpack this entry rather than using it as a file. The digest is still the digest of the archive's own bytes. For a model that is a directory — a piper voice is an .onnx plus several hundred phoneme tables the runtime opens by directory path.

variant.description: The `variants[].name` this file belongs to. Absent means every variant, which is how a tokeniser shared by an int8 and an fp32 build is declared once.

params.description: Runtime knobs. Values naming a file map that file to what the runtime expects — the only way to find anything in a content-addressed store.

superseded_by.description: The id of the model that replaces this one. A catalogue may hide a superseded model that is not installed, and must keep showing one that is: it is what earlier releases put on people's disks.

gated.description: true when the upstream host requires a credential before it will serve these files. Summo asks for one rather than reporting a download failure it cannot explain.

variants.description: The builds this model ships, when it ships more than one. A file with no `variant` tag belongs to every variant, so a tokeniser is declared once. Summo picks by platform, then by the accelerator this machine has, then by what the publisher measured, then by precision against free memory.

name.description: Referenced by the `variant` on each file, e.g. `int8` or `coreml`.

accel.description: Absent means this build runs anywhere the platform does.

preferred.description: Set when the publisher has measured the builds against one another and this one won. It overrules the precision rule, which is only a guess: quantising SenseVoice costs a tenth of a point of word error rate and saves 700 MB, while quantising Whisper tiny costs seven and a half points and is slower. Neither is derivable from a manifest, so the manifest states it.
